title: Spiritual Renewal
english: As we find ourselves in a state of spiritual dedication and pleasant circumstances, we are actually opposing the entire royal nature, which is accustomed to rejoicing together in celebrating the Savior's wonders beyond all understanding, and in praising our Savior's achievements that surpass all wonder.

The present season is indeed spring, a time of renewal and rebirth, and it seems to me that many are able to eloquently express themselves with a well-trodden tongue, but with a most excellent mind, they can truly step into the depths of wisdom, for I think that many can step on the word with a tongue that is fluent, yet with a mind that is most excellent.

For now, the harsh face of winter has been wiped away, and the clear suns shine brightly, illuminating the mountains and valleys, forests and meadows, which are once again restored to their most beautiful state, being in a state of spiritual dedication and pleasant circumstances.

The shepherd, filled with joy, plays a sweet melody on the flute, releasing a clear sound that echoes through the blooming and newly grown grass, as he lets his flock graze freely, and he releases the flock, and the ewe, having given birth, grazes together with her lamb, under the watchful eye of the cowherd.

The vine, with its new shoots, stretches out like fingers, touching the grown plants, and the beauty of the grapes will soon be revealed, and the meadows, fragrant with the scent of flowers, delight the farmers with the usual gift of their bounty, and someone could add countless other things to these, honoring the time of blossoming.

As the plants grow, so too does the nature that governs all things on earth, namely humanity, rise with them, and this is evident in the spring, which brings us the resurrection of our Savior, through which all people are remade into new life, having overcome the corruption of death, and through which we are all remade into newness of life.

The power of God, who gives life to all things, is what allows plant species and kinds to return to their original appearance, while humanity, without any care from above, lies lifeless, and however, the time has come for us to renew all of nature, which is superior to all things on earth, and this is made possible by Christ, the creator of this renewal, who spoke through one of the prophets, saying, 'Take courage, Zion, do not let your hands weaken, for the Lord God is powerful in you, will save you, and renew you in his love' (Isaiah 35:3-4).

This renewal is a result of God's love for us, which was demonstrated when he became human for us, remaking all of nature in himself into new life and restoring it to its original state, as God, showing us a spiritual spring.

If someone wants to learn and is eager to know clearly, and to know what is revealed from both, and what the difference is between the psychic and spiritual, I will quote Paul, saying, 'The psychic person does not accept the things of the Spirit of God' (1 Corinthians 2:14), highlighting the difference between the psychic and spiritual, and the spiritual person examines all things, and he himself examines, but he is not examined by anyone.

Foolishness is a state of being that prevents one from understanding that they are being spiritually examined, and in contrast, the spiritual person has the ability to examine all things, and he examines, but he himself is not subject to examination by anyone, for they have learned to discern everything in a straightforward and simple manner, without being swayed by the desires of the soul.

Those who yield to the laws of the Spirit and allow themselves to be guided by them are able to overcome the things that would otherwise hinder them, and they are not afraid to test what is beneficial and to prefer what is useful over what is pleasant, and they strive to place what is advantageous after what is not, and they are not judged by anyone, but rather they discern all things for themselves, and the spiritual person examines, and he is not examined by anyone.

For who, tell me, of those who have chosen to live in this way, would not rather condemn their own wickedness, and define the most shameful things as their own, for to foolishly tolerate evil is a demonstration of the utmost worthlessness, and the one who does not refuse to advocate for such shameful things will himself be a witness to his own vileness, through the things by which he knew how to honor what he should have rebuked as evil.

The divine Scripture determines that no one is inferior in weakness, and this is because he cannot discern the natures of things correctly, and as it is written, 'Woe to those who say good is evil and evil is good, who put darkness as light and light as darkness' (Isaiah 5:20), and such behavior is not characteristic of those who are good and spiritual, but rather of those who are fleshly and evil.

For those who are controlled by the pleasures of the present life are so far removed from wanting to do good that they even ignore what is good, and however, as lovers of God and spiritual people, we must present ourselves as living from the dead to Christ, who died and rose for us, and as the divine Paul commands us, 'If we live by the Spirit, let us also walk by the Spirit' (Galatians 5:25).

Let us not be drawn to alien pleasures or shameful desires, but rather look towards the heavenly Jerusalem, which is our mother, and let us live a life of meekness and vigilance, and with upright and unwavering faith, let us honor our Master, having in mind the written word, 'You shall love the Lord your God with your whole soul and whole strength' (Deuteronomy 6:5, Matthew 22:37), and He sets the measure of love for all of us, commanding to honor with complete faith, not thinking the faith is weak or incomplete for piety.

The Lord says, 'You shall have no other gods before Me' (Exodus 20:3, Deuteronomy 5:7), and it is easy to fall into apostasy and corruption, which is a proof of littleness of soul, and it is ridiculous to be seen as worthless.

The word of God is for those who are perfected through sympathy and exercise, and it is the elements and principles of the words of God, and as our Savior says, 'The healthy do not need a doctor, but the sick do' (Matthew 9:12, Mark 2:17, Luke 5:31), and the one with a strong heart will stand even without encouragement, but the weak-hearted needs a lot of help.

The word will come to us through examples, for plants with deep roots, having been firmly established with strong foundations, grow upwards to great heights and are not affected by the excesses of the winds, and even when surrounded by a strong and irresistible gust of wind, they remain safely preserved, but trees that have not grown very thick, being still tender and newly sprouted, would require many supports to prevent them from being overturned, for there is so much weakness in them, and also a shortness of time, and their stance is so precarious that they can be overturned by a single gust of wind…

title: Faithfulness and Deception
english: It is as if one is cast down from the foundations, but young men who are recently in their prime are laid in the same manner.
Those who have already attained a safe and truly god-loving mind, and are rooted in faith in God, remain unshaken, even as Satan tempts them.
On the other hand, those who still have a heart that indulges in luxury would easily fall away, unless they often receive corrective words.
If such people were not in my midst, I would have spoken directly to those who are trained.
But since I see many who are undecided, I must address them.
It is time to say to them, as Paul did, "Beware, brothers and sisters, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God." (Hebrews 3:12)
If we must say something openly, let us approach faith without pretence, with a whole heart and mind.
No one can serve two masters, for either they will hate one and love the other, or they will be devoted to one and despise the other.

As we consider the story of someone who was taken captive by barbarians at a young age and raised among them, we see how they adopted the customs and habits of their captors, but also struggled with the ingrained values of their homeland.

As this person grew in understanding and maturity, they began to recognize the truth about their situation and longed for their beloved homeland and desired to be instructed in the paternal laws that had been passed down to them.
Eventually, they presented themselves to the king and stated the reasons for their actions, and as a result, they were deemed worthy of honor and old age.

The question arises, then, whether such a person, still barbarized and thinking like their captors, would reasonably be expected to be punished, or whether they would be worthy of greater things due to their faithfulness and goodwill.
Let us return to the beginning of the human race and examine the things concerning the first-formed man.
He was full of every good and had reached the highest peak of joy within us, of which he was also master, unless he had transgressed the divine commandment out of deception.
The first of the sons born from him, together with him, offered the firstfruits of what they had found, for nature knew how to honor God, needing no law for this.
Abel offered sacrifices from his flock, while Cain did so from the fruits of the earth.
For Abel was a shepherd, and it seemed good to Cain to cultivate the earth, and he did this.

But as the human race always slid towards what is worse, and suffered a more shameful evil than what had gone before, the law that had been sown in nature was destroyed and trampled, although it persuaded God to give the one and only.
Moreover, the error of polytheism was added to all the other evils, a terrible teaching, a peak of the devil's bitterness.
It was thus, and not otherwise, that our affairs were led to complete destruction, and we were excluded from friendship with God due to the sin that was introduced.
As we naturally incline towards God, we fear that we may be shaken off from his greed and drawn to the ancient beauty of our own nature.
However, this desire has been corrupted by false worship, which has clothed humanity in a kind of slavery.
The free person has become a slave, as it were, to the whims of their own desires.
But this deceitful hunt will not succeed, for it is not possible for humanity to reach the end of things according to its own mind.
The cowardly person fights against God out of ignorance, and suffers the same fate as sailors who cling to the winds and are destroyed by their own ship.
In contrast, the only-begotten Word of God has shone upon us, freeing us from the bonds of sin and showing us to be free instead of captives.
This is the ancient and innate knowledge of the one and true God, which has been corrupted by the foreign and harmful invention of worshiping many gods.
We do not pay homage to the sun, moon, stars, earth, and water, for we have been given the name of divinity and have written down a multitude of gods.
Having been redeemed through Christ, we remain faithful and true worshippers of the one who has been honored.
We must not be deceived by empty words, nor have unfaithfulness in our minds, lest we be found to be pretentious outwardly while hiding an idolater within.
If one still has a barbaric mindset, what does it mean to claim royal thoughts?
The law knows the assistant of freedom, not the traitor.
One who genuinely struggles and is unwilling to conquer opponents is not double-minded and abominable.
Even the Greek poets have spoken similarly, and one would agree that it is correct.
However, they are haughty and sacrilegious, and they call themselves by other names, which seems to me to be a beautiful way of thinking.
I have heard one of them say clearly that those who conceive one thing and express another are equal to the gates of Hades.
For deceit and fraud are truly accursed and easily refuted, and they accuse the worst of all vices.
What is the point of silence, and why do you conceal in darkness the things that you hold dear in your mind?
Is it not the case that you are eager to hide, and that this hiding is motivated by the shame that you would feel if your true nature were to be revealed?

For it is characteristic of someone who is trying to hide their flaws to conceal the things for which they would be justly criticized, and to lack the brightness that comes from being open and honest.
If you are aware of the things that are worthy of wonder, and you are sane, then why do you not make yourself known to all, and reveal your true nature?

If you are ashamed of the things that are hidden within you, and you use a veil to conceal the invisible aspects of your character, then you are seeking glory through a false pretense, and this is more honorable than the things that are rightly believed.
Why do you not speak to others about these things, and find yourself radiant and confident, speaking as a brother to those who are inwardly focused, and as a relative to those who are…

title: Hypocrisy and the Love of Victory
english: When we are convinced to think in words, we become simple and full of praise, going to the extreme. This simplicity is rooted in a deep understanding of the truth, and it is this understanding that allows us to stand against the love of victory and the empty words that often accompany it. The unanimous confession to Christ from all sides is a powerful testament to the truth, and it is this truth that we must hold onto, even when faced with opposition and criticism.

The love of victory and the desire for praise can lead us down a path of hypocrisy, where we honor God with our lips but our hearts are far from him. This is a dangerous path, one that can lead to a superficial show of reverence, where we use polished words and empty phrases to pretend a devotion that we do not truly feel. But God sees through this hypocrisy, and he will not be fooled by our empty words. As the prophet Isaiah so eloquently puts it, the people come near to God, they honor him with their lips, but their heart is far from him, and they worship him in vain.

If someone thinks they can deceive others without facing the consequences, and does not fear the severe punishment that comes with lying to God, then they should revere duplicity and consider the one who introduces lies to be wandering aimlessly. However, if a penalty is indeed established for those who engage in such behavior, and punishment, justice, and all forms of mistreatment await them, along with unquenchable fire that will consume even the unwilling, then how can the person who sees the greater madness - being controlled by intemperate pleasure - not prioritize their own soul?

For the love of pleasure is the greatest passion, and it is good to acknowledge the danger that it poses. One might detect a plot or present their own strength, even if it is less than the other's, or compete beyond their power, but ultimately, they will be saved in another way. But tell me, how can someone escape the wrath of God? Where can they flee to be saved? Even if we attribute great brilliance to their life, it will not surpass the divine standard. Let them be surrounded by abundant wealth, rivaling the famous and unparalleled wealth of Croesus, but will they find rest? They will leave these things behind, not willingly, but because the punisher demands it. The divine Scripture will not lie, saying that treasures will not benefit the lawless, and therefore, it is not terrible to approach God.

Let us demonstrate once again how God views the double-minded as wicked. He considers them to be boasters and insolent, and He insults those who are alienated from Him. This is evident in His words to Jeremiah, where He reproaches the Israelites for their apostasies, saying, 'You saw what the house of Israel did to me; they went to every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and they committed fornication there.' Here, the Scripture uses the term 'fornication' to describe their devotion to the demons. This is a common way for the divine Scripture to speak.

The Israelites would take the wooded mountain peaks and create cuts and altars under the dense trees. At times, they would rise up a little mound and offer libations and sacrifices to the demonic trees and to the nymphs, or perhaps to the Baal revered by them. They would do all sorts of shameful things, and God is grieved by their boldness. Although they were educated by the law, they yielded to the devil, pleasing their own desires and rejecting the commandment that sobers their heart. The Master of all says to the prophet Jeremiah, 'Shear your head, and throw away, and take up a lament on your lips, because the Lord has rejected and cast away the generation that did these things.' By commanding the prophet to shear his head, God shows clearly what kind of justice those who sinned will undergo.

The fate of those who have fallen prey to the deceits of demons is akin to a hair being cut off from the body, leaving it alienated and without connection to its former whole. As a result, they are cut off from intimacy with God, and through divine wrath, they become of no concern, no longer worthy of care from above. The prayer of the saints, which is typically worthy of all consideration, is not applied to them alone, for it is said that one should not pray for this people or ask that they be shown mercy, as God will not listen.

This matter is so grave that even the greatest and most ancient figures, such as Moses and Samuel, would be of no use if they were to stand before God on behalf of this people. The Spirit-bearer is deeply grieved by this reality, and the prophet is bitter about the fact that prayer would be rejected and of no use. In response, God apologizes in a way, teaching that not even the most esteemed individuals would be able to change the situation. Someone might argue that secretly sinning would be less severe, but this mindset would be misguided, as it would still be rightly and justly condemned, and would still have reason to fear the God who watches over the hidden things.

Although someone might escape human notice, God's all-seeing eyes miss nothing. As the apostle Paul says, everything is laid bare before God's eyes, naked and uncovered. If it seems to you that those who sin secretly and those who sin openly provoke the same amount and kind of anger, I will teach you from the divine Scripture. You should receive this again into your mind and consider the fact that some of the ancients were deluded, despite knowing God and being guided by many writings towards the knowledge of truth.

They fashioned a multitude of idols and fell into dark and invisible places, where the disease of sin progressed slowly towards worse things. Even those who were entrusted with priestly duties were not immune to its effects. The matter was distressing and inaccessible to God, who intended to punish those who provoked Him by serving other gods. Through the prophet Ezekiel, God explains their daring deeds and shows them the truth, saying, 'Listen, and it happened in the sixth year, in the fifth month, on the fifth day of the month, I was sitting in my house, and the hand of the Lord was upon me, and I saw a vision of a man, from his waist down was fire, and from his waist up was like the appearance of electrum.'

As I stood there, a likeness of a hand stretched out and took me by the crown of my head, and a Spirit lifted me up between the earth and the heaven, bringing me to Jerusalem in a vision of God. Then, in a swift sequence of events, I was brought to the vestibule of the court, where I saw a remarkable sight. A single door appeared in the wall, and I was instructed to dig into the wall, which I did, and to my surprise, another door was revealed.

The Lord then commanded me to enter through this door and witness the wicked abominations that were being committed in that place. As I entered, I saw a shocking array of creeping things and beasts, all manner of vain and detestable abominations, and all around me, the idols of the sons of Israel were drawn, a stark reminder of the depths of their rebellion against God. Seventy of the elders of the house were present, and I was left to ponder the gravity of their actions.
